yahoofinancer — Recipes

Source: yahoofinancer-recipes.md

Short, self-contained workflows. Each recipe assumes the package is installed and loaded. Copy, paste, run.

install.packages("yahoofinancer")
library(yahoofinancer)

1. Fetch daily prices for one stock

The most common starting point. Returns a data.frame with date, open, high, low, close, adjusted close, and volume.

aapl <- Ticker$new("AAPL")

prices <- aapl$get_history(
  start    = "2024-01-01",
  end      = "2024-12-31",
  interval = "1d"
)

head(prices)

Tip: interval accepts "1d", "1wk", or "1mo" for daily, weekly, and monthly bars. Use period = "1y" instead of start/end for a rolling window relative to today.

2. Fetch prices for multiple tickers at once

Use the Tickers class to pull several symbols in one object. A failed symbol is skipped gracefully; the rest still return.

tickers <- Tickers$new(c("AAPL", "MSFT", "GOOGL", "AMZN"))

prices <- tickers$get_history(
  start    = "2024-01-01",
  interval = "1d"
)

# symbol column lets you split or filter easily
head(prices[prices$symbol == "MSFT", ])

3. Plot cumulative returns for a portfolio

Pairs naturally with recipe 2. Normalises each stock to 100 at the start date so you can compare apples to apples.

library(ggplot2)

tickers <- Tickers$new(c("AAPL", "MSFT", "GOOGL"))
prices  <- tickers$get_history(start = "2024-01-01", interval = "1d")

# compute cumulative return indexed to 100
prices <- prices[order(prices$symbol, prices$date), ]
prices$cum_return <- ave(
  prices$close,
  prices$symbol,
  FUN = function(x) x / x[1] * 100
)

ggplot(prices, aes(x = as.Date(date), y = cum_return, colour = symbol)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
  labs(
    title  = "Cumulative return (indexed to 100)",
    x      = NULL,
    y      = "Index value",
    colour = NULL
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

4. Get a real-time quote

regular_market_price reflects the last traded price during market hours (or the closing price outside hours). No history call needed.

aapl  <- Ticker$new("AAPL")
tsla  <- Ticker$new("TSLA")

cat("AAPL:", aapl$regular_market_price, "\n")
cat("TSLA:", tsla$regular_market_price, "\n")

For many tickers at once, use the market summary or loop over a Tickers object. get_market_summary() returns a snapshot of major indices.

get_market_summary()

5. Validate symbols before a bulk download

Passing a bad ticker to Tickers wastes a network call and can produce confusing empty data.frames. Run validate() first.

symbols <- c("AAPL", "NOTASTOCK", "MSFT", "XYZXYZ")

good <- validate(symbols)  # returns the subset that Yahoo Finance recognises
cat("Valid symbols:", paste(good, collapse = ", "), "\n")

tickers <- Tickers$new(good)
prices  <- tickers$get_history(start = "2024-01-01", interval = "1d")

6. Pull a key metrics snapshot for stock screening

key_stats surfaces financial ratios — trailing P/E, forward P/E, price-to-book, enterprise value, and more — as a named list. Flatten to a one-row data.frame for easy comparison across tickers.

symbols <- c("AAPL", "MSFT", "GOOGL", "META")

stats <- lapply(symbols, function(sym) {
  t   <- Ticker$new(sym)
  ks  <- t$key_stats
  data.frame(
    symbol       = sym,
    pe_trailing  = ks$trailingPE,
    pe_forward   = ks$forwardPE,
    price_book   = ks$priceToBook,
    profit_margin = ks$profitMargins,
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
})

do.call(rbind, stats)

7. Retrieve analyst recommendations

recommendations shows the symbols that Yahoo Finance users who viewed this stock also hold, along with a similarity score. upgrade_downgrade_history gives the richer analyst ratings timeline.

aapl <- Ticker$new("AAPL")

# "people also watch" recommendations
aapl$recommendations

# analyst upgrade / downgrade history
upgrades <- aapl$upgrade_downgrade_history
head(upgrades[order(upgrades$epochGradeDate, decreasing = TRUE), ])

8. Convert currencies with historical rates

currency_converter() is a standalone function — no Ticker object needed. Returns the same OHLCV data.frame format as stock history.

# spot rate today
currency_converter(from = "GBP", to = "USD", period = "1d", interval = "1d")

# historical daily rates for the past year
gbp_usd <- currency_converter(
  from     = "GBP",
  to       = "USD",
  start    = "2024-01-01",
  end      = "2024-12-31",
  interval = "1d"
)

plot(as.Date(gbp_usd$date), gbp_usd$close,
     type = "l", xlab = "", ylab = "GBP/USD", main = "GBP/USD — 2024")

9. Fetch index data (e.g. S&P 500, Nifty 50)

Use the Index class with the Yahoo Finance symbol for the index (prefixed with ^). The API is identical to Ticker.

# Common index symbols:
#   ^GSPC  S&P 500
#   ^IXIC  NASDAQ Composite
#   ^DJI   Dow Jones Industrial Average
#   ^NSEI  Nifty 50
#   ^FTSE  FTSE 100

sp500 <- Index$new("^GSPC")

sp500_prices <- sp500$get_history(
  start    = "2023-01-01",
  interval = "1wk"
)

tail(sp500_prices)

10. Extract earnings dates and EPS history

earnings returns both historical actuals and forward estimates — useful for event studies and earnings-surprise analysis.

aapl <- Ticker$new("AAPL")

earnings <- aapl$earnings

# quarterly EPS actuals vs estimates
earnings$earningsChart$quarterly

# annual revenue and earnings
earnings$financialsChart$yearly

Tip: Pair with get_history() using a narrow window around each earnings date to compute price reactions.

11. Retrieve ESG / sustainability scores

ESG data is surfaced through the esg_scores property. Not every ticker has scores — check for NULL before using.

symbols <- c("AAPL", "MSFT", "XOM", "TSLA")

esg <- lapply(symbols, function(sym) {
  t <- Ticker$new(sym)
  s <- t$esg_scores
  if (is.null(s)) return(NULL)
  data.frame(
    symbol        = sym,
    total_esg     = s$totalEsg,
    environment   = s$environmentScore,
    social        = s$socialScore,
    governance    = s$governanceScore,
    peer_group    = s$peerGroup,
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
})

do.call(rbind, Filter(Negate(is.null), esg))

12. List trending tickers by country

get_trending() surfaces the securities currently trending on Yahoo Finance for a given market. Useful as a universe filter or for momentum screens.

# "US" for United States, "GB" for UK, "IN" for India, etc.
trending_us <- get_trending("US")
head(trending_us)

13. Get top executives and their compensation

company_officers returns the executive roster with title, age, year born, fiscal year, and total pay — useful for governance research.

aapl <- Ticker$new("AAPL")

officers <- aapl$company_officers
officers[, c("name", "title", "total_pay")]

14. Compare income statements across companies

income_statement() (via financials) returns a data.frame of annual or quarterly income statement items. Use lapply to build a cross-company comparison table.

symbols <- c("AAPL", "MSFT", "GOOGL")

revenue <- lapply(symbols, function(sym) {
  t  <- Ticker$new(sym)
  fs <- t$income_statement(frequency = "annual")
  if (is.null(fs) || nrow(fs) == 0) return(NULL)
  # most recent year
  row <- fs[1, , drop = FALSE]
  data.frame(
    symbol       = sym,
    year         = format(as.Date(row$asOfDate), "%Y"),
    total_revenue = row$TotalRevenue,
    net_income    = row$NetIncome,
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
})

do.call(rbind, Filter(Negate(is.null), revenue))

15. Build a minimal stock-screener pipeline

Combines several recipes into a tidy dplyr pipeline: validate symbols, fetch key stats, filter by criteria, and rank by a metric.

library(dplyr)

# candidate universe
symbols <- validate(c(
  "AAPL", "MSFT", "GOOGL", "META", "AMZN",
  "NVDA", "TSM",  "ASML", "ADBE", "CRM"
))

# fetch stats for each
stats <- lapply(symbols, function(sym) {
  tryCatch({
    t  <- Ticker$new(sym)
    ks <- t$key_stats
    data.frame(
      symbol        = sym,
      pe_forward    = ks$forwardPE      %||% NA_real_,
      price_book    = ks$priceToBook    %||% NA_real_,
      profit_margin = ks$profitMargins  %||% NA_real_,
      revenue_growth = ks$revenueGrowth %||% NA_real_,
      stringsAsFactors = FALSE
    )
  }, error = function(e) NULL)
})

screen <- do.call(rbind, Filter(Negate(is.null), stats))

# screen: profitable growth stocks trading below P/B of 15
screen |>
  filter(
    profit_margin  > 0.15,
    revenue_growth > 0.10,
    price_book     < 15
  ) |>
  arrange(pe_forward) |>
  select(symbol, pe_forward, price_book, profit_margin, revenue_growth)

Note: %||% is the null-coalescing operator from rlang (or define it locally: `%||%` <- function(a, b) if (is.null(a)) b else a).
